bugs.name: Return submission silently fails when refund reason is missing
bugs.summary: The return form enables its submit button without a required refund reason, then silently ignores submission until a reason is selected.
bugs.expected: The form disables submission or displays Reason is required when the mandatory refund reason is missing.
bugs.actual: The enabled button initially leaves the page at /return with no error, notification, or operation. Selecting Damaged Item makes the same submission succeed and records the refund. Reproduced on two orders, including a simple return without replacement or shipping refund.
reproSteps: Sign in and open a paid, fulfilled order with a returnable line item.
Click Set maximal quantities to select a quantity of 1.
Enable Grant refund and select the paid transaction.
Leave the lower Refund Reason selector at its placeholder.
Select Damaged Item in the Refund Reason selector and click Return and Replace products again.
bugs.reason: Submitting without a refund reason visibly marks the reason selector red before any return/refund request; selecting Damaged Item allows the return. The claimed absence of validation feedback is false.

bugs.name: Manual transaction silently ignores a negative amount
bugs.summary: The manual capture dialog leaves its action enabled for a negative amount but provides no validation feedback when submitted.
bugs.expected: A negative capture amount is rejected with a clear validation error or the submit action is disabled.
bugs.actual: For -1 and -10 the enabled Add manual capture button leaves the dialog open unchanged, with no amount error and no transaction. Positive 1 succeeds immediately and creates a Manual capture transaction.
reproSteps: Sign in and open an order detail page.
Enter a description and set Transaction amount to -1.
Repeat with -10, then try a positive amount of 1.
bugs.reason: For both -1 and -10, clicking Add manual capture shows the native visible validation message 'Value must be greater than or equal to 0.' Positive1 creates the transaction; the alleged silent rejection does not occur.

bugs.name: Edited order-history comment temporarily remains alongside original text
bugs.summary: The report calls the original comment remaining beside its edited entry a temporary display defect. Order History intentionally preserves the original note and adds a linked edit event; independent UI verification retained both after reload.
bugs.expected: After Save succeeds, the timeline should immediately reflect the edited comment without continuing to show its old text as a separate current entry.
bugs.actual: The report claims the edited comment and original added entry remained together for over 29 seconds, and that refreshing the same order left only the edited entry.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture administrator, open Fulfillment > Drafts, and create a disposable draft in Channel-USD.
In Order History, add a uniquely named comment and submit it.
Hover over that comment, click its pencil edit control, replace the text with a different unique comment, and click Save.
Inspect the original added entry and linked edited entry, then reload the same draft. The report claims the original disappears after reload.
bugs.reason: Human review confirmed this is intentional edit history, not a bug. Updating an order note creates a new event linked to the original rather than replacing or deleting it. The pinned backend test explicitly requires both events, and the dashboard’s edited-note link points back to the original entry. Independent UI verification showed both entries remained after reload, contradicting the report’s claimed temporary disappearance. Preserving the original alongside the edited entry is correct behavior.
